title: El-Ganzouri Risk Index (Difficult Airway)
sources: el-Ganzouri AR et al. Anesth Analg 1996; simplified airway risk index (SARI)
purpose: A weighted seven-factor preoperative score for predicting difficult laryngoscopy / intubation. A score ≥ 4 predicts difficulty and should trigger an explicit difficult-airway plan (awake technique, videolaryngoscopy first, senior help, equipment at hand).

items.label: Ability to prognath (advance lower incisors past upper)

interpretation.label: Lower predicted risk of difficult laryngoscopy — proceed with a standard induction plan, but keep a rescue strategy and videolaryngoscope available (no score rules out difficulty)

Predicted difficult airway — formulate an explicit plan: consider an awake / videolaryngoscopy-first approach, ensure a skilled assistant and difficult-airway cart, optimise position and preoxygenation, and have a surgical-airway plan (front-of-neck access) briefed

notes: The index misses several important predictors — limited neck extension from a collar/fixed flexion deformity, airway masses/radiation, beard, oedema, blood/secretions, and the physiologically difficult airway (hypoxaemia, hypotension, acidosis). Bedside gestalt plus this score, not the score alone. Videolaryngoscopy reduces but does not eliminate the failure rate in high scorers.
buildNote: Additive, 7 weighted items. Threshold ≥ 4 predicts difficulty.
